<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" />{{GHGcorrected}}</noinclude><section begin="par70" />{{GHGmargin-letter|70|c}}
Rem. 1. The only verbs of this kind are: {{GHGheb|text=יָטַב|translate=to be good}} (only in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} and in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}; in the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=טוֹב}}, a verb {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, is used instead), {{GHGheb|text=יָנַק|translate=to suck}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָקַץ|translate=to awake}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָצַר|translate=to form}} (but see above, a), {{GHGheb|text=יָלַל}} only in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵילִיל|translate=to bewail}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָשַׁר|translate=to be straight, right}}, also {{GHGheb|text=יָבֵשׁ}} (Arabic ''yăbĭsă'') ''to be dry'' (but {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הוֹבִישׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=6}}, on the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}; on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=5}}, cf. {{GHGpar|72|x}}), and the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵימִין}} (denominative from {{GHGheb|text=יָמִין}}), infin. {{GHGheb|text=לְהֵמִין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=19}} ''to go to the right''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|70|d}}
2. In some examples of the {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} the preformative has been subsequently added to the contracted form: {{GHGheb|text=יְיֵטִיב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְיֵלִיל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=15|verse=2.3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=16|verse=7|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֲיֵלִיל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=31}}; plur. {{GHGheb|text=יְיֵלִ֫ילוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=7|verse=14}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=65|verse=14}}. Qimḥi and others explain the above forms from a phonetic interchange of {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} and ''He'', arising from the unsyncopated forms {{GHGheb|text=יְהֵילִיל}}, &c. (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=52|verse=5}}). It is, perhaps, more correct to suppose that the regular forms ({{GHGheb|text=יֵיטִיב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יֵילִיל}}) were originally intended, but that in the later pronunciation the syllable was broken up in order to restore artificially the preformative which had become merged in the first radical.

{{GHGmargin-letter|70|e}}
Isolated anomalies are: {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהֵיטִֽבֹתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=11}} with separating vowel (for {{GHGheb|text=הֵיטַ֫בְתִּי}}) on the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}; {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יֵיטֵיב}} for {{GHGheb|text=יֵיטִיב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=47}}; {{GHGheb|text=תֵּֽיטְבִי}} ({{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} for {{GHGheb|text=תִּיטְבִי}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּנִיקֵ֫הוּ}} {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=9}}, either an error for {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּֽינִק׳}}, or an irregular shortening of the first syllable, caused by the forward movement of the tone. Similarly, the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵקִיץ}} (from {{GHGheb|text=קוּץ}}) is always used instead of {{GHGheb|text=הֵיקִיץ}} from {{GHGheb|text=יָקַץ}}; hence also {{GHGheb|text=הֲקִיצ֫וֹתָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֱקִיצֹ֫תִי}}, ''imperat.'' {{GHGheb|text=הָקִ֫יצָה}}, ''infin.'' {{GHGheb|text=הָקִיץ}}.—On {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּבְּשֵׁ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=1|verse=4}}, see {{GHGpar|69|u}}).
<section end="par70" />
<section begin="par71" />{{GHGpar-heading|71|Verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}}. Third Class, or Verbs with Yôdh assimilated}}

In some verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״י}}, the {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} (or the original {{GHGterm|Wāw}}) does not quiesce in the preceding vowel, but is regarded as a full consonant, and, like ''Nûn'',<ref>These verbs, like verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} (cf. above, note on {{GHGpar|67|g}}), may perhaps have been influenced by the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ן}}.</ref> is assimilated to the following consonant. These forms, therefore, belong properly to the class of strong verbs. Assimilation invariably takes place in {{GHGheb|text=יָצַע}} (prop. {{GHGheb|text=וצע}}) ''to spread under''; {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִצִּיעַ}}, {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הֻצַּע}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָצַת|translate=to burn}}, imperfect {{GHGheb|text=יִצַּת}}, {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נִצַּת}}, {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִצִּית}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=4}} also {{GHGheb|text=אַצִּיתֶ֫נָּה}} is to be read with König; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=30}} the Masora has rightly emended the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=והוציתיה}}, which could only be the 1st sing. perf. of a verb {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}, to the imperative {{GHGheb|text=וְהַצִּית֫וּהָ}} in agreement with the context and all the early versions); {{GHGheb|text=יָצַג}}, {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִצִּיג|translate=to place}}, {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הֻצַּג}}; and probably also in the forms ordinarily derived from {{GHGheb|text=נָצַב}}, viz. {{GHGheb|text=נִצַּב}} ({{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}), {{GHGheb|text=הִצִּיב}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַצִּיב}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֻצַּב}}; at any rate a stem {{GHGheb|text=יָצַב}} is implied by the {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִתְיַצֵּב}}; instead of the anomalous {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּֽתַצַּב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=4}} read with the Samaritan {{GHGheb|text=ותתיצב}}, i.e. {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּתְיַצֵּב}}. Besides the common form we find once {{GHGheb|text=אֶצֹּק}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=3}} (from {{GHGheb|text=יָצַק|translate=to pour}}) with a ''transitive'' meaning, beside {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּ֫צֶק}} i''ntransitive'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=35}}. Elsewhere the {{GHGterm|imperfect}}<section end="par71" /><noinclude>
